records.category: supervisory failure; penalties on banks not imposed and the statutory sanctions commission not activated
records.people: no individual is named; the finding is against the Banque Centrale de Tunisie as an institution and the Cour des comptes as the finding body
records.summary: Tunisia's Cour des comptes, in the thirty-second edition of its annual report as reported on 11 February 2021, found that the Banque Centrale de Tunisie supervised the banking sector laxly: it had not imposed penalties it could have imposed on banks, which the report quantifies as 123.12 million dinars over governance and internal-control breaches and 47.8 million dinars over anti-money-laundering breaches, had not finalised the implementing texts of the banking law, and had not published its sanction rules. The second source named below adds that the Cour found the bank had not activated the sanctions commission provided for by the banking law, and that provisions on the effective global interest rate were unclear and incompatible with Law No. 99-64 of 15 July 1999. The BCT answered that the sums are what it could have imposed rather than fines waived, and that it had not adopted a punitive approach.
records.detail: This is a second and separate Tunisian episode from the one the map already holds, which is the 2018 arrest of five central bank agents for money laundering (tsa-algerie.com). It is also distinct from the two Tunisian records on the removals-and-pressure row, the June 2012 dismissal and the February 2024 law obliging the bank to lend to the treasury. The finding is a supervisory failure by the bank, which this project counts, rather than the bank acting as detector. Both sources read are press summaries of the Cour des comptes' report and not the primary document: Business News Tunisia, 11 February 2021 (the source_url), and Managers.tn, 11 February 2021, 'La BCT: tous les depassements ne sont pas automatiquement sanctionnes' (https://managers.tn/2021/02/11/la-bct-tous-les-depassements-ne-sont-pas-automatiquement-sanctionnes/), which carries the sanctions-commission and interest-rate findings and the BCT's communique in reply. The 123.12 and 47.8 million dinar figures and the description of the report as the thirty-second annual report come from the source_url page; the sanctions-commission finding comes from the Managers.tn page named here. No date other than the 11 February 2021 publication date carried by both pages is asserted: neither page states the date the Cour handed over or published the report, so none is given here. Round 71 read only a 2017 press summary of the thirtieth annual report, which named no BCT finding; the Cour's own report PDF was still not located this round.
records.source_title: Business News Tunisia, 11 February 2021 - Cour des comptes report on the Banque Centrale de Tunisie's supervision of the banking sector

records.central_bank: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)
records.category: suspected graft referred against an official of a central bank subsidiary; no case opened and no prosecution
records.people: an anonymised former deputy director of the Central Mint (named only as 'A jun' in the published report); the Central Mint of China, a Central Bank of the Republic of China subsidiary; the Central Bank's own ethics office; the Ministry of Justice Agency Against Corruption; the Taipei District Prosecutors Office
records.summary: The Control Yuan's published investigation report on the Central Mint of China, a subsidiary of Taiwan's central bank, records that after the central bank found a power cable running from a plant socket to the private car of the Mint's deputy director during a routine property check, the Mint's own ethics office judged that criminal liability might be involved and that the conduct might amount to graft, and referred the case through the Central Bank's ethics office to the Ministry of Justice Agency Against Corruption. The report states that the Agency Against Corruption judged that the matter involved no official-duty conduct and no offence of graft, so it opened no investigation and returned the case to the Central Bank's ethics office to be handled as an ordinary unlawful-act matter, and that the Taipei District Prosecutors Office issued a decision not to prosecute the electricity-theft offence the official had reported himself for, on the ground of insufficient suspicion.
records.detail: A second and separate Taiwanese episode from the one the map holds, which is the 2019 Mirror Media report of questioned procurement at the Central Engraving and Printing Plant, a different subsidiary, with different actors and a different year. Dates on the source page are written in the Republic of China calendar, and the conversions given here are arithmetic on those printed values and nothing more: the property check is dated 111 nian 8 yue 11 ri (11 August 2022), the two-demerit penalty 111 nian 8 yue 31 ri (31 August 2022), the Central Bank's dismissal of the official's administrative appeal 112 nian 11 yue 6 ri (6 November 2023), and the prosecutors' non-prosecution decision 113 nian 5 yue 13 ri (13 May 2024). The source_url serves a Microsoft Word document rather than a PDF, which is how the Control Yuan publishes the public version of this report; a date-checking script fetching it must read it as a .docx. Two further Control Yuan documents on the same matter were downloaded and read and are named here as second sources: the corrective-measure text against the Central Mint, 114 cai zheng 2, at https://multimedia.cy.gov.tw/DocFiles/IFDEWebBBS_CY/Docs/114/3RD/00/37/Attach/114caizheng2-gonggao-v1.docx (the live path uses backslashes and the Chinese characters cai zheng), which corrects the Mint for failing to investigate a workplace-bullying complaint under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and the Ministry of Labor's guidance revised on 111 nian 8 yue 18 ri (18 August 2022) and calls the handling a clear dereliction; and the Finance and Economics Committee's closure table at https://cybsbox.cy.gov.tw/CYBSBoxSSL/edoc/download/72060, which records the Central Bank stating that the Mint's handling of the complaint left room for improvement and the committee resolving on 114.06.04 (4 June 2025) to close the corrective case. Only the graft referral and its closure are filed as the case here; the bullying-handling dereliction is an official finding against the subsidiary but is not corruption, so it is reported in notes rather than filed as a case.
records.quote: 法務部廉政署判斷本件未涉職務行為，亦非涉貪瀆罪名
records.source_title: Control Yuan of the Republic of China, published investigation report on the Central Mint of China (public version), case on the penalising of an employee and the handling of his complaint

blanks.note: Two primary Cour des comptes de Madagascar documents were downloaded and read in full, which is the first time Madagascar has actually been tested on this vein. (1) 'Rapport sur l'audit des flux financiers lies a la lutte contre la COVID-19, gestion 2020', dated February 2022, 851,141 bytes, https://www.aisccuf.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/rapport-cour-des-comptes.pdf: grepped for 'Banque Centrale', 'Banky Foiben', 'Foiben' and 'BFM' and every one of the twenty-odd hits was read in context. The Banque Centrale de Madagascar appears throughout only as the Treasury's banker - the opening of the designated USD project account by BFM letter of 9 April 2020, the credit and debit advices, the two FCR retrocession conventions signed between the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the BCM on 4 June and 16 September 2020, and the delayed sale of foreign currency in December 2020 and January 2021. Every finding in those passages runs against the MEF and the ACCTDP for leaving funds unconverted and for requesting the currency sale late, not against the bank. There is no finding whose subject is the BCM, and on this project's rule that makes it not even a counterparty-only record worth filing. (2) 'La Cour des comptes publie son rapport de performance 2022', 1,877,471 bytes, https://www.aisccuf.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/la-cour-des-comptes-publie-son-rapport-de-performance-20221696501227.pdf: 24,543 characters of extractable text, and the word 'banque' occurs twice, both times meaning the World Bank as a funder of the Cour's own projects. No BFM or BCM mention at all. The Cour's own complete report index on its official site was still not opened, so the vein is closed on these two documents rather than on the institution.

Round 71's named next step was opened and it does not carry what was hoped. The Tribunal de Contas de Angola's own 'fiscalizacao sucessiva' page, https://tcontas.ao/en/fiscalizacao/sucessiva, was fetched and read. It is not the per-entity list the inversion test needs: it names no audited entity at all, describing only the process by which the Tribunal 'selecciona a cada ano civil, os servicos ou entidades sujeitas a sua jurisdicao', and the only documents it names are Resolucao 3-20 on the regulation of concomitant oversight and Lei n.o 13-10 of 9 July on the Tribunal's organisation and procedure. The Banco Nacional de Angola does not appear on the page in any form. So the inversion test still cannot be performed for Angola from this page, and the route that remains is the 'Relatorios e Contas TCA' section the page links in its navigation, which was not opened for want of budget. Angola's single record is still the '500 milhoes' conviction.

One primary-ish document was read and it narrows the vein sharply. Institute for Public Policy Research, 'The Role of the Auditor-General in Tackling Corruption', 2020, by Dietrich Remmert, https://ippr.org.na/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/Final-AG-Paper.pdf, 2,019,125 bytes, 76,615 characters of text, downloaded and grepped in full. It sets out the Auditor-General's mandate under the State Finance Act 31 of 1991 over government ministries, authorities, agencies and statutory bodies, discusses the office's coverage of 38 public enterprises, statutory bodies, funds and trade accounts, and surveys the office's reports. The strings 'Bank of Namibia' and 'central bank' do not occur anywhere in the document. That is a study of the Auditor-General's work that never mentions the central bank, which is consistent with the Bank of Namibia not being among the bodies the Auditor-General audits, and it is the reason no Auditor-General report on the Bank of Namibia has been identified in two rounds. It is a strong indication rather than a settled inversion test, because the document is a think-tank study and not the Auditor-General's own list of audited bodies, which was not reached. Note that this is also a weak-source-class document and nothing was filed from it.

Searched in English for court and Auditor-General findings naming the National Bank of Rwanda and both leads were opened or attempted and both fail the row's subject test. (1) The Rwanda Law Reports High Court judgment the search returned, https://decisia.judiciary.gov.rw/rlr/hc/en/346817/1/document.do, returned a 114-byte JSON body with status 404 and error 'Not Found' to curl, so it was not read and not retried for want of budget. (2) New Times, 'Thirteen in court over botched Rwf1bn fraud', https://www.newtimes.co.rw/article/150279/News/thirteen-in-court-over-botched-rwf1bn-fraud/amp, was read: the hack of 27 November 2017 targeted Access Bank Rwanda's account held at the National Bank of Rwanda, the accused include Access Bank Rwanda's own head of ICT, Olubunmi Adebisi Jaiyeula, and the hearing opened on 4 April 2018 at the Nyarugenge Intermediate Court with a further hearing set for 8 June 2018. The subject is Access Bank Rwanda and its staff, not the BNR, its officials or its own money, so this is not filable even as counterparty-only. Rwanda's one record remains the 2014 Rwf63m staff fraud. The Office of the Auditor General's own annual audit report series on oag.gov.rw, which search surfaced as press releases and as the 2023, 2024 and 2025 presentations to Parliament, was not opened and is the document for the next round.

Round 71's host note is stale and this is the finding to carry forward. The al.gov.mo attachment paths that the search returns for 'Relatorio de Auditoria' no longer serve documents: three of them, https://www.al.gov.mo/uploads/attachment/2019-10/147835d9e8dada5659.pdf, https://www.al.gov.mo/uploads/attachment/2023-10/710776539e1544d56d.pdf and https://al.gov.mo/uploads/attachment/2025-10/8547368ff2aca9865f.pdf, each returned an identical 117-byte body to plain curl with zero extractable text, and the third, tried again through WebFetch, returned an HTML page whose entire content is a zero-second meta refresh to the relative path /zh-hant/index.html. So neither tool reaches an al.gov.mo attachment at present and the Comissariado da Auditoria's per-subject reports were not tested. The gov.mo annual policy-lines documents for 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2026 were surfaced by the search and not opened, round 71 having already shown that the 2024 edition carries no list of audited entities, so no inversion test exists for Macao and the country is still untested on this vein.
